messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `PD-INC-11247` — private-control-plane: agent-heartbeat-missing for customer `acme-prod`. Severity: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INCIDENTS/PD-INC-11247

pagerduty-bot: Trigger details: control-plane reports no heartbeat from on-prem agent `acme-agent-02` since 2026-03-14T02:12:30Z. Retries failed (3/3).

jessica: acked and taking this. pinging oncall. Starting initial triage — grabbing control plane logs and last heartbeat timestamp.

mike: seeing same alert in cloudwatch for the customer's private control plane proxy — latency spikes right before loss.

jessica: jumping into the runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/private-agent-heartbeat.md — step 1: verify agent process + 2: check network peering.

ryan: I can check customer VPC peer and route tables. on it now.

jessica: i've pulled control-plane logs, here's tail of the agent registry:```
[2026-03-14T02:10:24Z] INFO registered agent acme-agent-02 v1.3.4
[2026-03-14T02:12:25Z] WARN missed heartbeat from acme-agent-02
[2026-03-14T02:12:30Z] ERROR connection closed: timeout
[2026-03-14T02:12:30Z] INFO initiating health-check probe to 10.8.5.12:443
[2026-03-14T02:12:35Z] ERROR probe failed: connection refused
```

support-sam: support ticket #78421 (customer ACME) shows they started seeing "model unavailable" errors at 02:12 UTC. Customer-facing note queued.

mike: interesting — control plane probe to 10.8.5.12:443 failing. that IP is the on-prem NAT for acme. could be firewall/peering.

ryan: quick checks on GCP peering: `gcloud compute routes list --filter="network:acme-vpc"` shows routes intact. VPC peering status *looks* UP. I'll run a connectivity test from our egress node to 10.8.5.12.

ryan: running `nc -vz 10.8.5.12 443` from redwood-egress-3... result: `Connection timed out`.

jessica: i'm going to attempt a soft restart on the agent via the customer-side management endpoint (we have emergency SSH key). executing:```
ssh admin@10.8.5.12 sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 --no-pager
```

incident-bot: :pager: Escalation: not acknowledged by SRE lead in 10m -> escalated to `sre-lead`.

sre-lead: on-call handover accepted. Joining. any evidence of kernel panic or full disk on agent host?

jessica: after restart, journal shows agent crashed with OOM right before heartbeat stopped:```
Mar 14 02:11:57 acme-agent-02 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2411 (python3) score 872 or sacrifice child
Mar 14 02:12:01 acme-agent-02 systemd[1]: redwood-agent.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Mar 14 02:12:05 acme-agent-02 systemd[1]: redwood-agent.service: failed with result 'signal'
```

mike: OOM + connection refused explains it. need to check if customer's on-prem monitoring has any recent infra changes (cron job, backup).

support-sam: customer replies: "We had a backup window that hit at 02:10 UTC — it spiked IO." They're verifying backup duration.

eng-private: note — we recently pushed a minor agent change (v1.3.4) that increases memory under load in a small window; coordinating with infra. but OOM aligns with backup time.

jessica: mitigation: 1) we restarted agent (recovered), 2) temporary throttle configured on agent to limit worker count until customer adjusts backup timing. applying config now via management API:```
PATCH https://private-controlplane.acme/api/v1/agents/acme-agent-02/config
{"max_workers": 2, "memory_limit_mb": 1024}
```

jessica: config applied, agent back online. heartbeat regained at 02:21:09Z.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-INC-11247 acknowledged by jessica and sre-lead.

sre-lead: confirming customer impact — all ACME prod inference requests failed between 02:12:30Z and 02:21:09Z (~8m40s). recorded as partial outage for that customer only.

support-sam: sent update to customer: apology + mitigation steps + asking for reschedule of backup or staggering. ticket updated: https://support.redwood/acme/78421

mike: adding temporary alert: `private-agent-memory-usage > 85%` set to warn earlier. also flagging agent for postmortem inspection.

jessica: quick timeline for postmortem note: root cause = on-prem OOM during customer backup + recent agent memory increase under load. temporary mitigation applied (worker throttle). next steps: coordinate with eng-private to release patch with lower memory footprint and add stronger memory cgroup enforcement.

sre-lead: scheduling follow-up: postmortem doc + retro meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC. I'll create incident page and assign owners.

jessica: closing slack thread — will update once postmortem page is ready. :white_check_mark:

mike: thx team.

incident-bot: Incident PD-INC-11247 marked resolved at 1763234883.
